title: A second bishop must account for stewards and certify Saints for Zion
setting: Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon traveled from Hiram to Kirtland, Ohio, on 3 December 1831. The next day high priests and members met there to learn their duties. Joseph dictated three revelations that day, later printed together as this section. The first called the Kirtland merchant Newel K. Whitney as bishop in Ohio, while Edward Partridge served as bishop in Missouri. The other two set Whitney’s duties and rules for moving to Zion.
summary: The first revelation tells the high priests at Kirtland that a bishop is needed in this region. Elders here must account for their stewardship to him, with records sent to the bishop in Zion. It names Newel K. Whitney as that bishop. The second revelation sets his duties: keep the storehouse, receive funds, and supply the elders. Debts elders cannot pay go to the bishop in Zion, and their spiritual labors answer for them. Elders need this bishop’s certificate to be accepted in Zion, and publishing stewards may claim his help. The third requires members moving to Zion to carry a certificate from three elders or a bishop.

contextNote.title: Accounting as the mark of a steward
contextNote.text: The Ohio church had grown, but its bishop, Edward Partridge, now lived in Missouri. Verse 2 supplies a local bishop for “this part of the Lord’s vineyard” in Ohio. Verse 3 explains why the conference acted wisely: every steward must give an account. Verse 4 links that account to a reward in the mansions of the Father. Verses 17–18 show the practical result, a certificate that makes a person acceptable in Zion. In this passage, a steward is someone who holds goods or work for the Lord and reports on it.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 71–75 includes this revelation’s teaching on stewardship. According to verses 3–5, to whom did the Kirtland elders give an account, and what did faithfulness prepare them for?
reviewNote: Read all 26 verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, 4 December 1831, and three revelations compiled. JSP has three documents (–A vv. 1–8, –B vv. 9–23, –C vv. 24–26); the –A page is cited, and the historical introductions were read on the Church Historian’s Press study-companion mirror. JSP: Whitney was ordained between –A and –B. Edward Partridge is not named in the text but the bishop in Zion is; he is included because the setting requires him. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes
